gen-dafont-college-gf-abeezee: Dynamic and authoritative, College gives every curve the full strength of a straight stem, with big counters in a tall lowercase. ABeeZee, a friendly sans, supplies the neon-tube softness that loosens the whole pairing.
gen-dafont-college-gf-aldrich: Thick, solid strokes up top, then rounded, cupped letters down below. College's big counters and uniform curves lead, while Aldrich keeps its x-height close to the cap height, so the text feels compact beneath the display.
gen-dafont-college-gf-alexandria: College draws round letters with walls every bit as strong as its straight ones. And Alexandria, with its wide c and short stems, gives that weight somewhere to rest.
gen-dafont-college-gf-amiko: Authoritative and dynamic, College holds every stroke at the same visual weight. Amiko, a modern sans whose terminals flare outward like tongs, adds the pairing its most striking touch, a lively counterpoint to the heading.
gen-dafont-college-gf-anek-bangla: College is dynamic and authoritative, drawn with no heavier downstrokes. Anek Bangla, a sans with wide, barely curled s curves, takes over below and keeps the text approachable and low-slung.
gen-dafont-college-gf-atkinson-hyperlegi: College brings plain unmodulated outlines, big counters, and a tall lowercase. Atkinson Hyperlegible then reads approachably for paragraph after paragraph, its wide-set s terminals and clipped capitals keeping each word distinct.
gen-dafont-college-gf-blinker: College lands hard, with stout curves and big counters in a tall lowercase. Blinker holds its line thickness steady, with open apertures and lowercase filling most of the height.
gen-dafont-college-gf-funnel-sans: College is dynamic and authoritative, its curves as sturdy as its straight stems. College is best at emphasis, while Funnel Sans, with its widely opened e, is best at quiet text.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-guntur: Authoritative and dynamic, College gives round letters the same strength as its straight stems. But Hind Guntur, tall and plain like steel cable, would carry pages of text without any shift in stroke weight.
gen-dafont-college-gf-karla: Karla reads modern and approachable, with a gaping c and a middle band so tall the lines look stocky. College's single-nib strokes keep a full page of Karla feeling sturdy.
